Thank you for all your help with Gyarados and Celebi, %PLAYERNAME%. Though it seems our work isn’t over yet—Team GO Rocket still has Lugia and Ho-Oh.
With the team leaders’ help, we managed to pinpoint Apex Shadow Ho-Oh’s location. For reasons unknown, Team GO Rocket’s keeping the two Pokémon in separate locations.
Perhaps they’ve bitten off more than they can chew with these two Legendary Pokémon? In any case, this makes things easier for us: we’ll save these Pokémon one at a time!
Great work saving Apex Shadow Ho-Oh, %PLAYERNAME%! It looks like it knows Sacred Fire, Ho-Oh’s signature move—yet this one’s Sacred Fire is somehow even more powerful!
I wonder what will happen if you purify it. Will it become even stronger?
I’m going to continue researching this incredible Pokémon. I’ll keep you posted on what I learn.
While I’m off, why don’t you train up your Pokémon and see what friends are available to help with Apex Shadow Lugia.
We’re going to need all the help we can get!
The team leaders and I will also continue our investigation into Apex Shadow Lugia’s whereabouts. I hope we’ll know more soon.
Do you have everything you need, %PLAYERNAME%? Potions? Revives? Snacks?
Saving Apex Shadow Lugia will be an even greater challenge, so be prepared.

The team leaders and I discovered that Team GO Rocket has hidden Apex Shadow Lugia away in a secret hideout, guarded by a gauntlet of Grunts—and standing with them is none other than Giovanni himself.
And while I have you, remember how I said I’d conduct more research into Apex Shadow Ho-Oh?
Well, it turns out that if you purify it, its Sacred Fire move will become immeasurably powerful.
Apex Purified Ho-Oh might be an incredible ally in our quest to save Apex Shadow Lugia.
These may just be some of the toughest battles you’ll face as a Pokémon Trainer yet. But I know you, above all else, are the one most prepared for the challenge.
You saved Apex Shadow Lugia from Team GO Rocket!
Just like Ho-Oh, Apex Shadow Lugia’s Aeroblast attack is more powerful than any I’ve ever seen.
And just like Apex Shadow Ho-Oh, I’m confident that its power will increase even more if you purify it.
Now, I’d say we’re overdue for a celebration! You’ve earned it.
Your recent accomplishments are no small feat!
Thanks again for all your help. I’m sure Lugia and Ho-Oh are grateful, too. Until our next adventure...let’s GO!

What’s that you’ve got, %PLAYERNAME%? Ah! Yes, I see—this appears to be a very old coin.  I picked one up myself, actually. There’s something mysterious about them...
Professor Willow? Can you hear me?
All right, %PLAYERNAME%—let’s get cracking! I’d like to find a few more coins, so why don’t we start looking around?
These coins are a little suspicious, but I can’t help feeling excited all the same! I believe a thorough investigation is in order.
We’ve got a lot of ground to cover—so I’ll start my search over there! Are you ready? Then let’s GO!
Oh—hello, Jacq! It was great hearing you speak at the World Pokémon Ecological Society conference the other day!
Thank you. Your lecture, "Strolling through the World of Pokémon," was fantastic, too!
%PLAYERNAME%, this is Jacq. He teaches biology at an academy in the Paldea region.
It’s very nice to meet you! Hm? Oh! That coin...!
Hm? Do you know something about this, Jacq?
I think I might... I know we were supposed to discuss Diglett, but can I get a rain check? This is something that I want to look into!
Of course! I’ll get right on researching this with %PLAYERNAME%. And I’ll be sure to take a video of the coin and share it with you soon.
Thank you! I’ll see you later, then. Happy exploring!

Hey, %PLAYERNAME%, great timing! Fancy doing a little investigation?

All these Ultra Wormholes we’ve encountered lately have got me thinking. Ultra Space is fascinating, sure, but there are places closer to home that still beg to be explored—like the fabled island of Dragonite!
Once, a Dragonite saved a shipwrecked man, taking him to a remote island—a paradise occupied solely by Dragonite. Doesn’t that sound like something, %PLAYERNAME%?
Imagine the unique ecosystem that island would have! It’d be a veritable treasure trove for scientific inquiry.
Questions are already rattling around in my head: what do Dragonite use their horns for? How quickly can they move in water? What kind of Berries do they—
Whoops. I’m getting ahead of myself. First, we need to do some baseline research on the Pokémon in question.
We might even find some clues about this Dragonite paradise!
Let’s start by observing Dratini, which can evolve into Dragonair and then Dragonite, %PLAYERNAME%!
Whoa! Look at how many Dratini you’ve caught, %PLAYERNAME%!
Did you know that in the past, Dratini was so rarely glimpsed that some called it the “Mirage Pokémon”?
And yet here you are with a whole host of them. They seem real enough to me!
You know, I read a report recently that a small colony of Dratini was found living underwater.
That would suggest that Dratini and its Evolutions like to live in groups.
And if that’s true...then the island of Dragonite could be real after all! First, though, we should learn more about Dratini’s Evolution, Dragonair.
Dragonair’s mystical appearance always leaves me in awe. In fact, this Pokémon is known for its gentle aura.
Some even call it divine! And for good reason—see the crystalline globes on its head and tail? Dragonair can use them to freely control the weather.
I bet that’d come in useful if you had, say, an island full of Dragonite that you wanted to keep hidden. Or if you were constantly forgetting your research notes outside on rainy days...
But that’s a me problem. Next, let’s help Dragonair evolve into the star of today’s studies—Dragonite!
Just like Dratini and Dragonair, Dragonite is an extremely rarely seen Pokémon. How lucky we are that we can study one today!
Dragonite is known as “the sea incarnate.” Incur the wrath of this normally calm Pokémon at your peril, because it will smash everything to smithereens before it’s satisfied.
Luckily for us, it’s typically a kindhearted Pokémon. If it spots a drowning person or Pokémon, Dragonite simply must help them—like that shipwrecked man I mentioned earlier today.
Why don’t we set sail and get looking for that island? Dragonite’ll surely bail us out if things go sideways!
I’m joking, I’m joking. Thanks for humoring me today, %PLAYERNAME%.
Even without weighing anchor, we learned more about Pokémon and found new ways to look at facts we already knew. I’d say that’s time well spent.
Though to be fair, I’d say that about any time we spend together. Heh. I’ll be in touch again soon, %PLAYERNAME%!
I just observed a curious sight.
Floating over there were vaguely human visages, and carved slabs of...clay?
Yet despite the differences between these apparitions, they had a similar air.
As with many mysterious things in this world, I suspect Pokémon to be behind this.
Assuming I am correct, I wish to catch them. Then perhaps Professor Willow can share his insight.
Where’s that old getup of mine—oh! Hey there, %PLAYERNAME%!
I’ve been thinking of what to wear to Spark’s upcoming costume party. A Litwick hat? A Pikachu onesie? I can’t have Candela outshine me again this year.
Speaking of masquerades—is that a Yamask AND a Galarian Yamask? I can’t disguise my excitement!
You know, they say Yamask carry masks that used to be their faces when they were human. Sometimes they look at them and cry.
And Galarian Yamask are supposedly formed when ancient clay tablets are drawn to vengeful spirits.
Somber origins, but don’t they set your curiosity ablaze? I wonder how Yamask feel now that they’ve become Pokémon. What sort of thoughts are running through their minds?
In the “spirit” of inquiry, why don’t you see what other Ghost-type Pokémon you can find? You might even come across more Yamask!
Professor Willow is certainly knowledgeable. We were right to seek his wisdom.
To think that Yamask and Galarian Yamask have such origins... Incredible.
I must thank you for catching them. With every day we spend together, I learn something new.
The Pokémon we’ve seen of late have been...dark, in a manner of speaking.
But as the Professor said, they are simply another mystery we researchers can illuminate with our findings. Fear need not be a component of exploring the unknown.
%PLAYERNAME%, I shall continue observing these Yamask as I ponder today’s events.
Perhaps you could investigate other Ghost-type Pokémon in the meantime.
And to repay Professor Willow, I could see if I possess a GO Ultra Recon Squad uniform in his size...
Ah, %PLAYERNAME%! Welcome back. I’ve just about finished my Yamask, erm, mask, inspired by you and Rhi! What’ve the two of you been up to?
Whoa, you’ve caught even more Ghost-type Pokémon! It’s starting to look like a haunted house around here—or a haunted lab.
Ghost-type Pokémon always remind me how much remains in the world for us to uncover. Where do Drifloon drift off to? Do Duskull really spirit away bad children? What powers a Golett?

With enough time and perseverance, I’m sure we researchers will find the answers to these questions and more. Or maybe they’ll be answered by an up-and-at-’em Trainer like you! When it comes to learning, jump in headfirst, I always say!
Though...maybe I should amend that motto to exclude Ultra Wormholes. Haha.
Thanks for the extra motivation today, %PLAYERNAME%. I’ll see you again soon!
Hoopa Unbound is said to be tremendously powerful—but I think you can handle it, Trainer.
It’s been a long adventure with Hoopa, but I think we’ve finally reached the end.
It’s almost bittersweet, don’t you think? But fret not—I’m sure more discoveries await!
Let’s keep adventuring through this world full of mysteries—you, me, and Hoopa!
Of course, this is all just a theory.
We’ll have to test it before reaching any proper conclusions!
Hey there, %PLAYERNAME%! It’s great to see you, as always.
I’m feeling especially refreshed today, as if a pleasant island breeze was following me. Maybe it’s the freshly squeezed Pinap Juice I had for breakfast?
Or maybe it’s because more and more Pokémon first discovered in the Alola region have been coming to visit me lately!
Do you know about the Alola region, %PLAYERNAME%? It’s a cluster of tropical islands, each with unique scenery and Pokémon.
Alola even has Pokémon whose appearances are different than their counterparts in other regions. You may have encountered some of them before!
Why don’t you try looking for some Pokémon that were first discovered in Alola while I rustle up another glass of juice? I’m sure we have a lot to learn about our visitors!
Good timing, %PLAYERNAME%! I just finished my juice.
Thanks for looking into the Alola region’s Pokémon! You’re as diligent as ever.
Let me take a look at what you’ve discovered. Hmm... It seems many of the Pokémon you just met can be found on Alola’s Melemele Island.
Melemele Island is where many of Alola’s Trainers begin their island challenge. It’s very fitting that the Pokémon you just met are also some of the first that young Trainers in Alola meet, too!
%PLAYERNAME%. I suspect you have already noticed, but Team GO Rocket seems to be assembling en masse again.
What shadowy schemes could those ruffians be plotting? They look to be glowering right at you.
Surely they couldn’t be thinking of absconding with the Ultra Beasts?
Or perhaps they’ve designs on Cosmoem. In its current state, I fear—
No. Anxious speculation will not avail us. Preventative measures must come first.
%PLAYERNAME%. Could you use your battling skills to send some of these Grunts away?
Huh. I thought there were more Team GO Rocket Grunts around earlier...
Oh, %PLAYERNAME%, it’s you! I guess I’ve got you to thank for getting those goons out of here.
Rhi says they may be taking an interest in our otherworldly visitors, huh?
I’m inclined to think they’re right. Good thing you’re here to save the day!
Keep flushing Team GO Rocket out, %PLAYERNAME%. Try looking for their Leaders next.
I’m sure you and Rhi can track them down!
Brilliant work, %PLAYERNAME%. You’ve managed to defeat Team GO Rocket’s Leaders.
I knew your superlative skills would lead you to victory. And you had the chance to speak with Professor Willow, correct? What did he have to say?
I see... Though I am pleased Professor Willow has corroborated my theory, I continue to be concerned for the Ultra Beasts and Cosmoem.
I take solace in knowing that we have dispersed the majority of Team GO Rocket, if nothing else.
Now, the time has come to challenge the man who sits atop the organization: Giovanni.
So, you sent Giovanni home with his tail between his legs? Just another day in the life for you, huh, %PLAYERNAME%?
It’s no easy feat to put Team GO Rocket back in their place, but you rose to the challenge.
Great job! Now take some well-deserved rest with your Pokémon.
I’ll be in touch again soon!
Still in a holding pattern with Cosmoem, %PLAYERNAME%? Not to worry—sometimes slow and steady is the way to go. I’ll be waiting right here, so come see me when you have an update to share.
Hey, %PLAYERNAME%! Good to see you again!
You know, I thought I smelled something sweet in the air today.
Did I spill Berry juice again, you ask? You wound me, %PLAYERNAME%! As if I’d ruin this snazzy new jacket!
Heh. In all seriousness, the smell was coming from outside.
Unfortunately, I didn’t have a chance to track down the source of the scent. But now that you’re here, maybe you can sniff it out!
Welcome back, %PLAYERNAME%. Seeing as you’ve got Teddiursa with you, I think I can connect the dots on what I was smelling earlier—honey!
Teddiursa likes to lick its palms after soaking them in honey, so it’s no wonder I caught a whiff.
That reminds me of a fun fact about Teddiursa’s Evolution, Ursaring.
With its ability to distinguish any aroma, Ursaring unfailingly finds all food buried deep underground. If only it was that easy for me to find lunch!
Why don’t you help Teddiursa evolve so you can see Ursaring’s sleuthing skills for yourself, %PLAYERNAME%?
I thought I heard something stomping about, and here you are, Ursaring in tow!
Here’s the thing about Ursaring—although it has a large body, it’s quite skilled at climbing trees. It eats and sleeps in the treetops.
Ah, to be an Ursaring... Imagine how much easier that’d make fieldwork—or picking Pinap Berries!
Ahem. Snacks aside, have you noticed there’s a full moon out early today?
Looks like Ursaring is staring at it, too. Think you can find out why, %PLAYERNAME%?
I’ve never seen one in these parts. What an incredible find! Hmm...
Maybe in the Hisui region of long ago, where Ursaluna was first discovered, the full moon played a part in how Ursaring evolved.
It’s theorized that Hisui's swampy terrain gave Ursaluna its burly physique and ability to manipulate peat at will.
What kind of food would suit a Pokémon accustomed to living in swamps? Grains? Beans? Cake?
Maybe I should get baking for some firsthand taste-testing. I bet Teddiursa could lend me some honey!
Ah—listen to me yammering on and on. Researching Pokémon first found in Hisui never fails to pique my curiosity about the past!
Thanks again for spending the day learning about Pokémon with me, %PLAYERNAME%. I can always count on you to make my work a little sweeter!

But nothing’s happened yet, so you just focus on having fun with your friends and your Pokémon!
It’s also the region where Dark- and Steel-type Pokémon were first discovered! Not to mention Mr. Pokémon and the mysterious Mystery Egg.
Speaking of Pokémon originally discovered in the Johto region, I’ve heard tell that Celebi, the Time Travel Pokémon, has been seen nearby.
Celebi has the ability to move through time.
I still can’t shake the feeling that Celebi had something to do with Hisuian Voltorb appearing in our time.
In any case, rumor has it this Celebi knows a special move. I hope we’ll get a chance to see if that’s true!
While you enjoy today’s festivities, keep vigilant for any signs of Team GO Rocket. I know I haven’t forgotten about them.
Hopefully we can get some insight into what they’ve been up to since they smashed open that mysterious door...
You know what your adventure needs, %PLAYERNAME%? A new buddy! I spoke with a colleague and was able to orchestrate a little surprise for you.
These Pokémon are the first partner Pokémon offered to Trainers in the Johto region. Go on—pick one!
I think that’s a great Pokémon, too, %PLAYERNAME%!
Chikorita, the Leaf Pokémon, is docile and loves to soak up the sun’s rays. A sweet aroma gently wafts from the leaf on its head. Doesn’t it have just the most adorable face?
Cyndaquil, the Fire Mouse Pokémon, is timid and always curls itself up in a ball. If attacked, it flares up its back for protection. Doesn’t its shyness make you want to cuddle it even more?
Totodile, the Big Jaw Pokémon, is small but rough and tough. It won’t hesitate to take a bite out of anything that moves. Though what’s the harm in one quick pet...
I’m sure this little one is eager to spend some time with you, and what better way than letting it join you on your Johto-inspired journey!
Wow, your Chikorita evolved into Bayleef already! And just in time, %PLAYERNAME%—I have some troubling news.
Wow, your Cyndaquil evolved into Quilava already! And just in time, %PLAYERNAME%—I have some troubling news.
Wow, your Totodile evolved into Croconaw already! And just in time, %PLAYERNAME%—I have some troubling news.
Team GO Rocket is mobilizing—and they’re headed straight toward us!
I have a feeling they’re stirring up more than just a mild bit of mischief... That must be why they’re launching an invasion—more distractions! Not to mention they always love to crash our parties.
Have they heard about the Celebi sightings? Or maybe they have something even more sinister up their sleeve...
I’m going to need your help defeating some Team GO Rocket Grunts—distract the distraction, and buy me some time to investigate. Can I count on your help?
Magnificent work, %PLAYERNAME%! While I was investigating, some Team GO Rocket Grunts ran by, whining about losing to an “unfairly strong Trainer.”
I assume you’re the Trainer in question? Haha, but of course! I knew I could trust you.
So, my sleuthing turned up an interesting rumor. A Gyarados has been spotted nearby, but it isn’t at all like your typical Gyarados.
This one seems like it’s mired in a fit of rage—not unlike a certain Red Gyarados that once rampaged the Johto region’s Lake of Rage.
